content:
The data runs to 2026-03-28, so these figures are 77 days old — treat them as a snapshot, not your current position.

The sharpest miss cuts in your favour. You guessed ≈£0 left to set aside. The real number was £960 — "worked out from what was left over, not from detected transfers." That's not a rounding error; the sketch was off by £960. **Eating out** landed the other way: you guessed ≈£150, the real spend was £19, a £131 undershoot. Your **housing**, **subscriptions**, and **bills** bands are still ≈ estimates — the upload couldn't isolate them, so they stay unverified.

On real numbers, your free cash flow is £513/month against a £2,300 net income and £1,787 in fixed costs. The exit pot needs £42/month to hit £1,000 by June 2028. That's less than 10% of your free cash. The sketch implied you had nothing spare; the real position is that the goal's monthly pace is already covered several times over.

With only 5 transactions across 87 days, the habits picture is thin but fillable — the timing, what's recurring, the patterns the sketch couldn't see are all visible now. What those patterns mean to you isn't something the data settles on its own. That's what the Value Map is for.

That check took me from a sketch to your real numbers — I now know you about 72%, past the 70% a real month unlocks. The last stretch is what these patterns mean to you, and that's what the Value Map settles.
